latest_release.body:
# Switchyard v0.4.0

Switchyard 0.4.0 adds decision model support, including Jev, independent Composite routing profiles, Plan/Execute through Stage Router, and application-defined target restrictions. It also expands the Python, TypeScript, and Go bindings and links benchmark results to the configurations used to produce them.

This release includes breaking changes for library users and existing routing configurations. Review the migration notes below before upgrading.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Switchyard/blob/v0.4.0/CHANGELOG.md#040) · [Changes since v0.3.0](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Switchyard/compare/v0.3.0...v0.4.0)

## Routing and integrations

- Decision models can make routing choices for standalone classifier routes, Stage judges, and Composite profile selection. Switchyard supports System One, the API used by Jev, alongside OpenAI Decisions. Configure the question, choices, and probability cutoff for selecting the capable or efficient model. [Jev example](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Switchyard/blob/v0.4.0/benchmark/routing-profiles/tb21-jev-opus-glm.toml) · [Decision model docs](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Switchyard/blob/v0.4.0/docs/protocols/decisions.md)
- Composite routing supports separate efficient-first and capable-first Stage profiles. An LLM classifier or decision model selects the starting profile, and the profile persists across compaction. Plan/Execute now runs through a Stage configuration. [Composite configuration](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Switchyard/blob/v0.4.0/docs/routing_algorithms/composite_routing.md)
- Applications can supply required labels to restrict routing to eligible targets. Requirements can persist across turns. The application classifies sensitive data and approves targets.
- Verification-Gated Routing (VGR) verifies a candidate answer from the efficient tier before choosing whether to serve it or fall back to the capable tier. It can escalate earlier after tool errors and fall back when Chat tool-call arguments are malformed.
- The DeepSWE benchmark guide links the published results to the tested Astra/Luna Plan/Execute profile and documents the workload, harness, and settings needed to reproduce the runs. [Benchmarks](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Switchyard/blob/v0.4.0/docs/benchmarks.md)

## Library and host APIs

- Python adds configured algorithm execution and streaming translation. TypeScript adds configured execution and buffered translation. Go supports native and WASM backends.
- Hosts can store and restore routing state across turns. Algorithms can run model and decision calls in parallel, and hosts can stop routing when they refuse a call. [Host integration guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Switchyard/blob/v0.4.0/docs/reference/host_integration.md)

## Compatibility and correctness

- Relay-managed buffered responses preserve upstream HTTP error statuses. Upstream error responses retain headers such as `Retry-After`.
- Translation preserves refusal details, streaming stop reasons, and plaintext Responses reasoning history for non-OpenAI targets. Chat requests that ask for multiple choices return an explicit error.
- Windowed classifiers drop empty history turns that could cause judge requests to fail.

## Migration and removals

- Move standalone Plan/Execute configurations to a Stage profile.
- The standalone server now binds to `127.0.0.1` by default. Set `--host` explicitly for deployments that accept remote clients.
- Rust and Python embedding callers must adopt the updated step-response APIs. Rust hosts now pass routing state into `Algorithm::run_stream` and receive the updated state in the routing outcome.
- Composite Stage profile settings and decision request fields have changed. Review the changelog for the replacement fields and removed Rust APIs.

## Install

Install the Python bindings:

```bash
pip install nemo-switchyard==0.4.0
```

Install the standalone server separately:

detail.readme:
# NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard

Switchyard is an open-source library that helps an AI agent choose which model handles each request. It combines efficient models with more capable models so you can balance task success, cost, and latency on your workload. Adopt Switchyard by embedding its Rust core, **libsy**, in your gateway or agent harness. You own the model clients, credentials, and service. Switchyard supplies the routing decision.

Quickstart  ·  Documentation  ·  Benchmarks  ·  What’s new  ·  Roadmap  ·  Releases  ·  Contributing

## How it works 1. Configure the models an agent can use and choose a routing algorithm. 2. The algorithm examines the request or the agent's recent tool activity. Some algorithms call a model to judge the task. 3. A gateway or agent sends the request to the selected model. Routing can change as the agent continues its work. Evaluate the complete agent, model pool, and routing configuration against your single-model baseline. A cheaper model call does not guarantee a cheaper successfully completed task. The [tuning loop](docs/tuning/index.md) gives the steps for that evaluation, and [Troubleshooting](docs/operations/troubleshooting.md) lists the settings that disable routing without an error. ## How to use it - **[Through an existing gateway](#through-an-existing-gateway):** Use an available gateway integration. - **[Embed libsy in your harness](#embed-libsy-in-your-harness):** Add libsy to a service you operate. - **[Evaluate Switchyard locally](#evaluate-switchyard-locally):** Compare routing configurations with your own model pool using the demo server. ### Through an existing gateway | Gateway | Start here | Deployment and limits | | --- | --- | --- | | **Agent Router** | [Agent Router](https://github.com/tetratelabs/built-on-envoy/blob/main/extensions/switchyard/README.md) | Open-source and self-hosted. It provides an OpenAI-compatible API and runs on Envoy. | | **LiteLLM** | [Run the Switchyard routing-plugin example](examples/litellm/README.md#quick-start-with-the-local-proxy) | Experimental and checkout-only. The example pins LiteLLM 1.102.0 and supports Stage routing based on request history, plus Random routing. It cannot service intermediate model calls required by classifier or escalation algorithms. | | **NeMo Relay** | [Build and configure the native plugin](crates/switchyard-nemo-relay-plugin/README.md#build-from-source) | Requires Relay `>=0.10.1, <1.0.0`. The source-build path requires a Rust toolchain and Python 3. | | **OpenRouter** | [Use Switchyard through OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/routers/switchyard-router) | Hosted by OpenRouter. Set `model` to `nvidia/switchyard` in API requests. | Relay 0.8.x and 0.9.0 can lose upstream error status and details when the plugin is enabled, even for models outside its routes. Review the [upstream error compatibility note](docs/integrations/nemo_relay.md#upstream-error-compatibility) before enabling the plugin. LiteLLM and NeMo Relay run in your own deployment. Follow each gateway's guidance for credentials and service operation. ### Embed libsy in your harness `Algorithm::run_stream` hands model calls and the final routing outcome back to your application. In this development-API outline, comments mark the work your code supplies: ```rust let mut steps = algorithm.run_stream(request, models, state); while let Some(step) = steps.next().await { match step? { Step::CallModel(call) => { // Send call.request through your LLM client. // Give the call future to call.respond(...).await. } Step::CallDecision(call) => { // Send call.request through your decision-model client. // Give its typed response future to call.respond(...).await. } Step::Done(outcome) => { match outcome.response { Some(response) => { // Return this answer; no final LLM call is needed. } None => { // Send outcome.request through your client for the final answer, // or pass it to your gateway to make that call later. } } } } } ``` - **Inputs:** supply an algorithm, model pool, request, and state. - **Calls:** your clients handle model calls. Stage returns a selection; other algorithms may return an answer. - **Start here:** [Rust quickstart](docs/getting_started.md) · [Python bindings](docs/reference/host_integration.md#python-bindings). ### Evaluate Switchyard locally The standalone server is provided only for demos and local evaluation. It is not a supported production deployment path. [Evaluate routing locally](docs/operations/local_evaluation.md) with the standalone server and your own model pool, then [verify routing is active](docs/operations/local_evaluation.md#verify-routing-is-active). The experimental [desktop and terminal quickstart](experimental/switchyard-desktop/README.md) covers local installation, coding-tool connections, sessions, usage, recovery, and uninstall. Agent-specific guides are available for [pi](docs/integrations/pi.md) and [Oh My Pi](docs/integrations/oh_my_pi.md). ## Routing algorithms Start with Auto. Choose Task, Execution, or Composite when you need more control. These names describe routing choices. The configuration keys are unchanged. | Choice | How it chooses | TOML configuration | | --- | --- | --- | | **[Auto](docs/routing_algorithms/overview.md#auto)** | Uses the current default: Execution (Stage), efficient-first, with a confidence threshold of 0.5 and no classifier call. | `type = "auto"` | | **[Task](docs/routing_algorithms/llm_classifier_routing.md)** | A model judges whether the efficient model can handle the task. | `type = "llm_classifier"`, `mode = "capability"` | | **[Execution](docs/routing_algorithms/stage_router_routing.md)** | Uses recent tool activity and outcome signals to choose a model as the agent runs. | `type = "stage_router"` | | **[Composite](docs/routing_algorithms/composite_routing.md)** | Combines Task and Execution: a classifier sets the default model tier when execution signals are uncertain. | `type = "composite"` | Auto is a fixed preset. It does not compare strategies at runtime. The TOML runner supports `type = "auto"`. In Rust, use `StageRouterConfig::new(PickerMode::EfficientFirst, 0.5)` for the same preset. The [routing overview](docs/routing_algorithms/overview.md) lists all strategies, including the [Plan/Execute configuration for Stage](docs/routing_algorithms/stage_router_routing.md#plan-and-execute), [escalation](docs/routing_algorithms/escalation_router_routing.md), [advisor](docs/routing_algorithms/advisor_gate_routing.md), [sub-agent](docs/routing_algorithms/subagent_routing.md), and [random](docs/routing_algorithms/random_routing.md). Integration support varies: check the gateway guide before choosing an algorithm. [Prefill routing](docs/routing_algorithms/prefill_routing.md) is designed for fast, efficient model selection using a model's prefill activations and a classifier trained on your own evaluation data. ## Evaluation and reference [Compare benchmark results and configs](docs/benchmarks.md) for Terminal-Bench 2.1 and DeepSWE. For latency and routing overhead testing, see [Soak Testing](docs/operations/soak_test.md). ### Further reading - [Benchmark setup and profiles](benchmark/README.md): run your own baseline and routing comparisons. - [Mechanics of Libsy](docs/mechanics_of_libsy.md): steps, model calls, and routing outcomes. - [TOML schema](docs/reference/toml_schema.md): configuration fields and defaults. - [Rust crate reference](docs/reference/rust_api.md): core and optional integration crates. - [Installation](INSTALLATION.md): package and platform requirements. ## Components Pre-1.0 software. APIs, configuration, and routing behavior can change between releases. Pin the version you integrate. | Component | Stability | Use it for | Guidance | |---|---|---|---| | `switchyard-libsy` | **Beta** | Routing embedded in your own gateway or harness. You own model calls, credentials, and retries. | Trial integrations. API will change before v1.0. | | `switchyard-llm-client` | **Alpha** | HTTP model calls and protocol translation alongside libsy. | Experiments and pilots. | | `switchyard-runner` | **Alpha** | Running configured routes inside another runtime, such as NeMo Relay. | Integration work and supervised pilots. | | `switchyard-server` | **Demo** | A standalone OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible proxy. | Demos and local evaluation only; not a supported production path. | ![Switchyard Components](docs/assets/switchyard-components.png) ## What’s new Features and integrations recently merged into `main`. - **2026-11-12 · Route Copilot Chat in VS Code**\ Pair a capable and an efficient model, and let Auto routing pick one for each request in Copilot Chat. [Setup guide →](examples/vscode/README.md) - **2026-10-16 · Route between Sonnet and Opus in Claude Code**\ Use your Claude login for automatic routing on Linux x86_64 and see the selected model in the status line. [Setup guide →](examples/claude/README.md) - **2026-10-15 · Use decision models in composite routing**\ Use Mercury Decide to judge tasks and Stage routing to adjust model selection as tools run. [Example configuration →](dev-server/config.toml) - **2026-10-13 · Use Jev to choose between models**\ Configure Jev as a task judge with candidate descriptions and a probability cutoff. [Configuration guide →](docs/routing_algorithms/composite_routing.md#decision-model-classifier) - **2026-10-12 · Bring Switchyard to TypeScript and Pi**\ Select models in Node.js or try automatic routing through Pi’s virtual models. [TypeScript bindings →](bindings/typescript/README.md) · [Pi example →](examples/pi/README.md) ## Community and license [Report an issue](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Switchyard/issues) · [Contribute](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [Code of conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) [Apache 2.0](LICENSE).
